definitions.variable: A symbol representing an unspecified or changing number.
definitions.constant: A value that does not vary in the given expression or model.
definitions.term: A single addend in an algebraic expression, including its sign.
definitions.coefficient: A numerical factor multiplying a variable or a variable product.
definitions.factor: A value or expression multiplied by another to form a product.
definitions.degree: The greatest exponent in a nonzero single-variable polynomial after simplification.
definitions.monomial: A polynomial consisting of exactly one nonzero term.
definitions.binomial: A polynomial consisting of exactly two nonzero terms after combining like terms.
definitions.trinomial: A polynomial consisting of exactly three nonzero terms after combining like terms.
definitions.polynomial: A finite sum of terms with variables raised to nonnegative integer powers.
definitions.standard form: A polynomial written with terms in descending order of power.
definitions.leading term: The highest-degree nonzero term when a polynomial is in standard form.
definitions.leading coefficient: The coefficient of the highest-degree nonzero term.
definitions.equivalent expressions: Different expressions yielding the same value for every input in their common domain.
definitions.commutative property: Changing the order of addition or multiplication does not change the result.
definitions.associative property: Regrouping numbers in addition or multiplication does not change the result.
definitions.distributive property: The rule a(b+c)=ab+ac, which also works in reverse for factoring.
definitions.identity: An equality true for all allowed values of its variables, or a value unchanged by an identity operation, depending on context.
definitions.inverse: An operation reversing another, such as addition and subtraction.
definitions.like terms: Terms that have identical variable factors and exponents, so their coefficients can be combined.
definitions.substitution: Replacing a variable with a specified number or expression.
definitions.greatest common factor: The largest positive integer factor dividing all of the listed integer coefficients or terms, as applicable.
definitions.factorization: Rewriting an expression as a product of factors.
